title: Dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson disease dementia

steps.tx: **Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB)** is the second most common neurodegenerative dementia after Alzheimer disease. When dementia starts before or within **1 year** of parkinsonism, the diagnosis is **DLB**, while dementia arising after **10 to 15 years** of established Parkinson disease is **Parkinson disease dementia (PDD)**. Both lie on a single **Lewy body disease** spectrum. About **10%** of Parkinson patients develop dementia each year, and most progress over time.

steps.tx: **Ageing** and **male sex** are the strongest risk factors for Lewy body disease. **GBA gene mutations** predispose to both PDD and DLB, while **alpha-synuclein gene duplications or triplications** produce Parkinson disease or DLB phenotypes. A long prodrome of **REM sleep behavior disorder**, anosmia, constipation, and depression often precedes diagnosis by years. Toxins acting on a susceptible genetic background are proposed as a **double hit**.

left.title: Genetic susceptibility

steps.tx: **Alpha-synuclein** misfolds into straight neurofilaments that form **Lewy bodies** and **Lewy neurites** in brainstem nuclei, amygdala, cingulate gyrus, and neocortex. Spread follows connected pathways from the **enteric nervous system** through the vagus nerve and from the **olfactory bulb** upward, in a prion-like manner. Profound **cholinergic loss** from basal forebrain degeneration causes the fluctuations, inattention, and visual hallucinations.

steps.tx: **Fluctuating attention and alertness** with episodes of confusion or lethargy is the signature cognitive pattern, with early deficits in **visuospatial and executive function** and relatively spared episodic memory. **Well-formed visual hallucinations** of people or animals appear early and are the single most characteristic feature. **Parkinsonism** with bradykinesia, rigidity, and early postural instability accompanies or follows the dementia.

steps.tx: **REM sleep behavior disorder** with violent dream enactment often predates dementia by years. **Severe neuroleptic sensitivity** means even small doses of typical antipsychotics can trigger rigidity or neuroleptic malignant syndrome. **Delusions** of misidentification and marked sensitivity to infections also occur. Alzheimer disease is predominantly **amnestic**, while **multiple system atrophy** shows earlier severe autonomic failure with preserved cognition.

steps.tx: **MRI brain** is the first test to exclude vascular parkinsonism, subdural collections, and strategic infarcts. **Dopamine transporter SPECT** showing reduced striatal uptake and **MIBG cardiac scintigraphy** showing sympathetic denervation are indicative biomarkers. **Polysomnography** shows REM sleep without atonia. The **gold standard** remains neuropathology with **alpha-synuclein immunostaining** of Lewy bodies and neurites.
steps.say: M R I brain is the first test to exclude vascular parkinsonism, subdural collections, and strategic infarcts. Dopamine transporter SPECT showing reduced striatal uptake and M I B G cardiac scintigraphy showing sympathetic denervation are indicative biomarkers. Polysomnography shows R E M sleep without atonia and helps confirm the disorder. The gold standard remains neuropathology with alpha-synuclein immunostaining of Lewy bodies and neurites.

steps.tx: **Rivastigmine** or **donepezil** is first line therapy for cognition and hallucinations, and the patch is re-titrated from **4.6 mg** per **24 hours** if more than **3 days** are missed. **Levodopa** is kept at the lowest effective dose for disabling parkinsonism. Refractory psychosis may need **clozapine** or **quetiapine** with extreme caution and blood monitoring, while **haloperidol** and anticholinergic drugs are avoided because they can cause death.
steps.say: Rivastigmine or donepezil is first line therapy for cognition and hallucinations, and the patch is re-titrated from the standard starting dose if more than three days are missed. Levodopa is kept at the lowest effective dose for disabling parkinsonism. Refractory psychosis may need clozapine or quetiapine with extreme caution and blood monitoring, while haloperidol and anticholinergic drugs are avoided because they can cause death.

steps.tx: **CSF alpha-synuclein RT-QuIC** seed amplification and cardiac **MIBG** imaging now support early diagnosis, alongside **DAT-SPECT** and occipital hypometabolism with the **cingulate island sign**. The **MCI with Lewy bodies** concept reflects prodromal disease with hallucinations, RBD, or fluctuations. Combining **levodopa** at the lowest effective dose with a cholinesterase inhibitor gives better motor tolerability.
steps.say: C S F alpha-synuclein R T Qu I C seed amplification and cardiac M I B G imaging now support early diagnosis, alongside D A T SPECT and occipital hypometabolism with the cingulate island sign. The M C I with Lewy bodies concept reflects prodromal disease with hallucinations, R B D, or fluctuations. Combining levodopa at the lowest effective dose with a cholinesterase inhibitor gives better motor tolerability.

steps.tx: Recurrent **falls** from postural instability cause fractures and head injury. **Aspiration pneumonia** and prolonged **delirium** during minor infections are common terminal events. Excessive daytime sleepiness and autonomic failure reduce independence. The course is steadily **progressive over years**, and coexistent Alzheimer pathology predicts faster decline. Structured physiotherapy, home safety review, and caregiver support reduce hospitalisation.

steps.tx: **High yield for the exam:** well-formed visual hallucinations mark DLB, the 1-year rule separates DLB from Parkinson disease dementia, violent RBD predates disease by years, DAT SPECT plus MIBG are indicative biomarkers, rivastigmine is first line therapy, haloperidol can cause death, and alpha-synuclein immunostaining is the gold standard.
